chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukayl, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding

a sheep which drank urine, then was slaughtered. He said: So he said: 'What is inside it shall be washed, then there is no problem with it; and similarly when it ate human excrement, as long as it had not become a dung-eater (jalala) — and the dung-eater (jalala) is one whose (regular) feed is that (filth).'

key_terms.بَوْل: Urine — classified as najis (ritually impure) in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.جَلَّالَة: Jalala — an animal whose primary food source is human excrement, rendering its meat and by-products prohibited until it undergoes istibra' (quarantine/purification period)
key_terms.جَوْف: The interior/belly of an animal — the contents must be washed before consumption
key_terms.عَذِرَة: Human excrement/feces — classified as najis (ritually impure)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/harm — a standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of a sheep that drank urine permissible in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issues a ruling on the ritual permissibility of consuming an animal that has ingested impure substances. If a sheep drank urine or ate human excrement on one occasion, its meat remains permissible after slaughter provided its stomach contents are washed; however, if the animal habitually subsists on such filth — making it a jalala — it would require a quarantine period before slaughter. This distinction between incidental and habitual consumption of najasah reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential framework for determining the ritual status of animal products.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Musa Bin Akeyl, from one of our companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a sheep which drank urine, then it was slaughtered. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is inside it would be washed, then there is no problem with it; and similar to that is when it were to eat the human excrement, and it does not happen to be a dung-eater, and the dung-eater is when that (dung) happens to be its (regular) feed’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from certain persons of our people from Ali ibn Hassa’n from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Musa ibn ‘Ukayl from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “About the case of a sheep that drinks urine, then is slaughtered, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The contents of its inside must be washed clean, then it is not unlawful, and also if it eats feces but is not a Jallal, which is an animal that has feces as its only feed.’”
